the following problems: (a) how to minimize a functional with a nearly flat gradient over vast regions; (b) how to minimize the functional so that the obtained result is a good approximation to a given image; (c) how to minimize it so that the obtained image has a desired histogram; (d) how to extend the algorithm to process colour images.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no algorithm that can be used to process digital images so that their histograms are exactly specified.
there is no method that can be applied to all images, that is, to all histograms, and that can be applied in a fast, efficient, and robust way to all of them.
, in the context of exact histogram specification, there is no method that can be considered as a universal tool for all types of images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel approach to compute minimizers of the l1-TV function for exact histogram specification.
we are able to compute a minimizer with an arbitrary precision using the same number of operations as the state-of-the art methods.
we propose to use a simple extension of the algorithm in [12] to compute the minimizers of a \({\mathbb L}^{1}\)-norm-based functional with a \({\cal C}^{2}\)-smoothed total-variation penalty term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to compute the minimizer of the \({\mathbf L}1\)-TV function with an arbitrary precision and with a fast and robust algorithm.
it is possible to design a fast algorithm to minimize the \({\mathbf{L}}_{1}\)-norm of the discrete gradient of a function, while preserving the exactness of the histogram.
